extracted.intended_audience: MSCA evaluation experts and peer reviewers (Rapporteurs, Evaluators, Vice-Chairs) assessing MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and assessment rubric for experts evaluating MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship (PF) proposals, covering the three main criteria (Excellence, Impact, Implementation), sub-criteria, consensus procedures, scoring, and rules for optional secondments/placements and other compliance issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the supervision between the researcher and the host
rubrics_metrics.description: quality of the supervision considering the qualifications and experience of the supervisor(s), their level of experience on the research topic proposed and their track record of work, including main international collaborations, as well as the level of experience in supervising/training especially at advanced level
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also evaluate effectiveness of planned training activities (scientific, management/organisation, horizontal and key transferrable skills). For European Fellowships assess the two-way transfer of knowledge between researcher and host; for Global Fellowships assess the three-way transfer involving associated partner for outgoing phase. If a non-academic placement is included its rationale and added value must be assessed under Excellence (1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale and added value of non-academic placement
rubrics_metrics.description: if applicable: the rationale and added value of the non-academic placement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals without non-academic placements are not to be penalised. The quality of the host arrangements and capacity of the non-academic placement host should be evaluated under Quality and Efficiency of the Implementation (3.2). A placement request must be substantiated by a letter of commitment from the non-academic organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum vitae and professional experience of the researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: curriculum vitae of the researcher, their professional experience, competences and skills
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under criterion 1.4 take into account information in the CV and the researcher’s overall track-record in relation to their level of experience. Evaluate quality and appropriateness of researcher’s existing professional experience in relation to the research proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1.4 Quality and appropriateness of the researcher’s professional experience, competences and skills
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposal includes a non-academic placement, its rationale and added-value must be assessed under 1.3. Proposals without non-academic placements are not to be penalised. Under criterion 1.4, take into account the CV and the researcher’s overall track-record in relation to their level of experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the researcher’s level (years of experience), track-record and how their competences match the proposed research. Use CV and Part B information to judge appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion 2: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPACT is about: the enhancement of the researcher’s career perspectives and skills development expected through the proposal implementation; dissemination, exploitation and communication of the research; direct scientific, societal and economic impact of the proposal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissemination = public disclosure of results; exploitation = use of results (e.g. commercial or policy). Communication/public engagement aims to inform society of activities and benefits. Assess overall expected impacts and plans to achieve them.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.1 Credibility of career and skills enhancement measures
rubrics_metrics.description: CREDIBILITY OF THE MEASURES TO ENHANCE THE CAREER PERSPECTIVES AND EMPLOYABILITY OF THE RESEARCHER AND CONTRIBUTION TO THEIR SKILLS DEVELOPMENT
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate expected career perspectives inside/outside academia, expected skills development, and whether measures are credible and likely to enhance employability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.2 Suitability and quality of dissemination, exploitation and communication measures
rubrics_metrics.description: SUITABILITY AND QUALITY OF THE MEASURES TO MAXIMISE EXPECTED OUTCOMES AND IMPACTS, AS SET OUT IN THE DISSEMINATION AND EXPLOITATION PLAN, INCLUDING COMMUNICATION ACTIVITIES
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess planned dissemination, exploitation and communication measures, target groups, and (if relevant) strategy for IP management. Measures must be concrete and proportionate to the scale of the project; evaluate planning of communication/public engagement (objectives, messages, tools, channels).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.3 Magnitude and importance of contribution to expected impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: THE MAGNITUDE AND IMPORTANCE OF THE PROJECT’S CONTRIBUTION TO THE EXPECTED SCIENTIFIC, SOCIETAL AND ECONOMIC IMPACTS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magnitude = how widespread outcomes/impacts likely are (e.g., size or proportion of target group benefiting). Importance = value of those benefits (e.g., additional healthy life years, efficiency savings). Evaluate credibility of quantified estimates of magnitude and importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion 3: Quality and Efficiency of the Implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: QUALITY AND EFFICIENCY OF THE IMPLEMENTATION is about: quality and effectiveness of the work plan; risk assessment and contingency plan; quality and capacity of all participating organisations, including non-scientific hosting arrangements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess completeness, feasibility and coherence of implementation arrangements across participating organisations and any non-academic hosting.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.1 Quality and effectiveness of the work plan and risk assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: QUALITY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF THE WORK PLAN, ASSESSMENT OF RISKS AND APPROPRIATENESS OF THE EFFORT ASSIGNED TO WORK PACKAGES
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate quality/effectiveness of the work plan (deliverables, milestones), appropriateness of effort assigned to work packages (timing, duration). For risk assessment, verify all possible risks have been identified and contingency measures proposed (including safety of researcher/family/participants). If risks have severe impact on implementation, reflect this in comments and scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.2 Quality and capacity of host institutions and participating organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: QUALITY AND CAPACITY OF THE HOST INSTITUTIONS AND PARTICIPATING ORGANISATIONS, INCLUDING HOSTING ARRANGEMENTS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check if a Gantt Chart is included (mandatory) and consistent with the work plan. Assess hosting arrangements (integration in team/institution, support services), infrastructure, logistics and facilities. For GF, consider both outgoing Third Country host and return host in EU MS/AC. For non-academic placements, evaluate placement host quality and capacity. Consider associated partners 'linked to a beneficiary' if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional secondments: duration and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may include an optional secondment phase within overall fellowship duration. For European PFs secondments cannot exceed one third of standard fellowship duration (12-24 months). For Global PFs optional secondments can be planned for up to one third of the outgoing phase, with additional restrictions (not during mandatory return period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposed periods exceed maximum duration, evaluate how proposal would be affected if secondment activities were within allowed duration and assess accordingly; may penalise under most appropriate criterion. If secondments lack relevance or added-value, reflect this in comments and scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional non-academic placement: eligibility and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral Fellowships proposals can include an additional optional period up to six months to support placements at non-academic organisations established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. The placement must be with a different non-academic host and be integral to the proposal, explaining added-value and backed by a letter of commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate placements for relevance and added-value; if placements are not properly described, lack relevance, are missing letter of commitment, are at an academic/third country organisation or otherwise ineligible, evaluate the proposal without considering the placement and reflect weaknesses accordingly (may affect final score). If Letter of Commitment does not fulfil minimum requirements (see Part B tech description sec 8), you may penalise under criterion 3.2. If in doubt about sector classification, treat organisation as non-academic and evaluate accordingly; if placement indicated does not meet requirements, either evaluate without it or inform VC/REA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Evaluation Form — Other questions (scope, exceptional funding, hE/hESC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of questions in Section 2 'Other questions' are not part of the evaluation criteria but provide important information for eligibility or subsequent evaluation steps (e.g. ethics, security). One exception: technical robustness of AI-based systems should be evaluated under Excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose 'in scope' by default (MSCA PF is bottom-up). Exceptional funding does not apply. For use of human embryos (hE) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC) you must state necessity; proposals involving hE/hESC can be funded only if their use is necessary to achieve objectives. Answers feed into ethics experts' assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities excluded from funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities that: aim at human cloning for reproductive purposes; intend to modify genetic heritage of human beings which could make such changes heritable (with specific exception for certain cancer treatment research); intend to create human embryos solely for research or stem cell procurement (e.g. by somatic cell nuclear transfer); lead to destruction of human embryos
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate under 'Activities excluded from funding' whether proposal includes any of these activities. If it does, immediately alert Vice-Chair and REA staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do No Significant Harm (DNSH) principle applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This does not apply to the MSCA PF call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tick 'not applicable' in the Proposal Evaluation Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive focus on civil applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the activities proposed have an exclusive focus on civil applications (activities intended for military applications or to serve military purposes cannot be funded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposal includes such activities, immediately alert Vice-Chair and REA staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial Intelligence — technical robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether activities involve use and/or development of AI-based systems and/or techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, assess the technical robustness of the proposed AI-system as part of the Excellence criterion (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall comments box usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Overall Comments box should only be used in case of excess pages and if the optional non-academic placement does not meet the requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Part B1 exceeds page limit insert standard remark that excess pages have been disregarded. If non-academic placement missing letter of commitment or is ineligible (third country or academic sector), insert the corresponding standard comment templates. Eligibility of a placement must be confirmed by REA during Grant Agreement Preparation if proposed for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics screening vs scientific evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: After scientific evaluation, proposals on the funding list or close to funding range will be screened by ethics experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT screen the proposal for ethical issues (except hESC/HE when asked). Comments related to ethics will not be included in scientific evaluation reports and consensus, and a proposal cannot be penalised on ethical grounds. However, the ethics section may include methodology and risks (e.g., safety) which scientific evaluators might use for risk assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission and overlap policy; scientific misconduct reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals submitted under the last H2020 call will not be treated as resubmissions under Horizon Europe calls. The researcher’s involvement in another running EU-funded grant should not influence your evaluation. Any suspicion of fabrication, falsification, plagiarism or other scientific misconduct must be reported to your Vice-Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat previous submissions as resubmissions for this call; avoid letting overlap with other grants bias assessment; report misconduct to Vice-Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: What if? — handling incompleteness, readability, eligibility concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposal seems incomplete, inform your Vice-Chair as soon as possible (it may be considered inadmissible). If difficult to read due to small font or other reasons, inform Vice-Chair so REA may ask applicant to reformat. If a Global Fellowship lacks a partner organisation letter of commitment it will be declared inadmissible. If potentially ineligible, continue evaluating and inform Vice-Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise issues promptly with Vice-Chair; continue evaluation even if you suspect ineligibility — REA staff will check eligibility during process. Examples of ineligibility indicators include no mobility, no PhD, more than allowed years of experience, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus phase aim and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The consensus phase (after IERs submitted) brings three evaluators together to agree on a Consensus Report (CR) and scores. The aim is to give a clear assessment of the proposal based on its merit, with examples; clear feedback on strengths and weaknesses of adequate length and appropriate tone; an explanation of shortcomings without making recommendations; and scores consistent with identified strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phase is conducted in SEP via the discussion box and/or teleconference. Roles: Rapporteur drafts CR and proposes scores; Evaluators participate to reach consensus; Vice-Chairs supervise and can assist. Use merge option to combine IERs; structure strengths and weaknesses per sub-criterion, avoid repetition; replace numbering with bullets in final CR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality requirements for the Consensus Report (CR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before moving to scoring ensure the final consensus report replaces numbering by bullets; comments express strengths and weaknesses (no descriptions or citations); all weaknesses are well justified; comments are concise and clear; there is no scientific 'advice' or recommendations; no mention of gender, name, nationality of individuals; no negative remarks as regards nationalities/cultures/countries; no overall remarks except standard sentences for excess pages; no references to previous evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vice-Chair will check fairness, objectivity and accuracy. Consult Annex for tips on CR quality. Use concise, justified bullet points, ensure tone is appropriate and compliant with prohibited content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring system and weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores from 0 to 5 (using one decimal) for each evaluation criterion. The proposal’s overall score is automatically calculated according to weights: Excellence 50%, Impact 30%, Implementation 20%. Score descriptors: 5 EXCELLENT (successfully addresses all relevant aspects; shortcomings minor), 4 VERY GOOD, 3 GOOD, 2 FAIR, 1 POOR, 0 FAIL (fails to address or cannot be assessed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full range with decimals (e.g., 3.3, 4.6). It is important that the scores reflect the comments (both strengths and weaknesses) agreed in the draft Consensus Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring process in SEP
rubrics_metrics.description: Rapporteur suggests scores that best reflect agreed comments and notifies Evaluators; Evaluators provide comments on proposed scores until agreement reached; after all agree the Rapporteur submits the CR in SEP for approval. If an Evaluator is not responsive notify VC and/or submit CR with a tentative score. Evaluators may 'approve' or 'disapprove' the CR and must leave reasons if disapproving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only after CR is approved by all three will Vice-Chair receive a 'draft ESR' for quality check. If Vice-Chair requests revisions, the CR may be sent back to consensus for revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOs for writing comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The comments must be: Relative to the proposal as it stands; Specific addressing each sub-criterion; In light of the type of action (EF or GF); Clear, substantial and concise; Consistent with the score awarded, which must reflect strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive qualifiers examples: timely, suited, very relevant, credible, very clear, precisely specified, realistic, very innovative, very well convincing, comprehensive, high quality, justified, strong, highly effective, thoughtful, very promising, evidence-based, well-formulated, fully in line, very profound, sound, very convincingly integrated, clearly articulated, coherent, well balanced, ambitious. Appropriate comment examples are provided in the guide (use concrete evidence and examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: DON'Ts for writing comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The comments must not be: A summary of the proposal; Too short, too long, inappropriate, discriminatory, politically incorrect; Categorical/general statements not properly verified; Based on assumptions; Recommendations or advice on improving the proposal; Contradictory statements relative to strengths and weaknesses; About the same weakness or strength under different criteria (no double penalization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mention real names of institutions, researchers and supervisors; avoid details that could lead to factual mistakes (page numbers, amounts, years). Avoid the expression 'is described' — explain whether something is 'fully' or 'poorly' described. Ethical issues should not be raised except when relevant (hESC/HE). Avoid offensive or subjective adjectives (awful, dreadful, terrible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency between comments and score (examples and anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure comments explain and justify the score (good comments explain it; poor comments merely echo the score or are vague/ambiguous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show poor vs good comments: e.g., 'The innovative aspects are poor' (poor) vs 'This proposal is not convincingly innovative in X and it does not properly take [xxx] into account' (good). Avoid ambiguity: replace 'probably inadequate' with precise statements and evidence. Make sure strengths/weaknesses and the numerical score align logically — large inconsistencies should be avoided.
